additions.reason: Line 3 of the source text states explicitly: 'וְיוֹם-טוֹב מֹחִין דְּאִמָּא, שֶׁהִיא בִּינָה.' This is unambiguous bechina language equating Yom Tov with Mochin deImma (the supernal mind of the Mother / Binah). The Rebbe establishes Yom Tov as a bechina of Binah — the 49 gates of Binah that Moshe attained led to humility; Yom Tov IS those Mochin deImma. In the dataset for Torah #135, 'יום טוב' appears only as part of compound node phrases (e.g. 'אור הגדול של יום טוב', 'קדשת יום טוב') but never as a standalone concept node with a bechina edge in its own right. The bechina יוֹם-טוֹב ↔ מֹחִין דְּאִמָּא / בִּינָה is the theological foundation of the entire Torah — it explains WHY receiving Yom Tov produces humility — yet it is absent from the bechina edge data for reference 135. This node belongs in Package 1 (מלכות/ענוה) because Yom Tov as Binah/Mochin deImma is the supernal source of the humility that flows into the domain of malkhut/yirah.

It belongs in Package 1 (מלכות/יראה) since it is the temporal-cosmic manifestation of the same quality: the awesome, judgment-laden, fearful aspect of holiness that IS the malkhut. Polarity is marked 'neutral' because ימי דין (days of judgment) is a structural feature that can apply either to the positive experience of the holy calendar or to the threatening presence of divine judgment — its full valence in Torah #135 is positive (these are days when malkhut dikdusha rises), but the concept itself is structurally neutral.
